vocab.note: Generated by `tools/katam/katam.mjs vocab` from committed C headers. No ROM data.

background.schema.json.title: katam background (katam-background/1)
background.schema.json.description: A parallax background layer (HW BG0): its tiles (indexed PNG), palette banks and tilemap. Shared by every room that names it.

offset.description: First BG palette entry written (colours; 96 = bank 6).

items.description: #RRGGBB; stored as BGR555 (5 bits per channel), so use multiples of 8 (+ low bits copied from the top: #RRGGBB = c5<<3|c5>>2 round-trips exactly).

bit15.description: Entries whose unused top bit is set (kept for exactness).

tilemap.description: One row per line, width tile tokens separated by spaces.

common.schema.json.title: Shared definitions for katam authoring files

roomRef.description: A room id, "room:<area>/<name>", e.g. "room:rainbow_route/126" (vanilla) or "room:my_mod/sky_garden". "room:vanilla/<number>" also resolves for vanilla rooms.

paletteRef.description: A foreground palette id, e.g. "palette:vanilla/29". Usually the same number as the tileset.

tileToken.description: One 8x8 tilemap entry, "TTTfP": TTT = tile index in hex (000-3ff), f = flip (. none, h horizontal, v vertical, x both), P = palette bank in hex. "000.0" is tile 0 unflipped in bank 0.

metatile.description: A 16x16 cell drawn as four 8x8 tile tokens, "TL TR BL BR", e.g. "001.0 002.0 021.0 022.0".

collisionValue.description: A collision (metatile attribute) value: an index 0-255 into the game's terrain table gCollisionAttributes. Named values come from the semantics registry.

gridRows.description: One string per row, top to bottom; each row is `width` legend keys concatenated (every key in a legend has the same length, 1 or 2 characters).

music.description: Background music, a name from game/include/constants/songs.h lowercased (e.g. "mus_rainbow_route"; a few vanilla rooms name an se_ entry), or a song number.

objectType.description: Object type: a name from game/include/constants/object_types.h without OBJ_, lowercased (e.g. "waddle_dee_1", "small_chest", "warp_star"), or the type number.

ability.description: A copy ability (game/include/constants/kirby.h without KIRBY_ABILITY_, lowercased), e.g. "fire", "sword"; "normal" = none.

object.schema.json.title: katam object type (katam-object/1)
object.schema.json.description: Per-type data of an enemy, item, gadget or boss: what the game keeps in a table (score, hit points, copy ability, tile budget). Behaviour is code; see docs/design/authoring/enemies.md.

numTiles.description: OBJ VRAM tiles reserved when it spawns.

raw.description: Descriptor fields by C name (unk0, unk1, unk2, unk4, unk8, pad0A).

code.description: ROM addresses of the type's constructor and animation bank: references to code, kept verbatim.

palette.schema.json.title: katam foreground palette (katam-palette/1)
palette.schema.json.description: The playfield's six 16-colour banks (BG palette banks 0-5). Colour 0 of each bank is transparent.

items.description: #RRGGBB; stored as BGR555 (5 bits per channel), so use multiples of 8 (+ low bits copied from the top: #RRGGBB = c5<<3|c5>>2 round-trips exactly).

vanillaRef.description: Palette-cycling animations are not decoded into the authoring format yet; this keeps the original's.

project.schema.json.title: katam project (katam-project/1)
project.schema.json.description: A folder of authoring files. A mod project names its base (usually the player's decompiled vanilla project) and adds or replaces resources by id.

base.description: "vanilla" for a mod on top of the game; compile/validate take the base folder with --base.

room.schema.json.title: katam room (katam-room/1)
room.schema.json.description: One room: its size, art, collision, objects, doors and properties. Coordinates: cells are 16x16 px, (0,0) top-left, x right, y down; objects are in pixels. A room is at least one screen (15x10 cells) and width*height must not exceed 1950 cells. See docs/design/authoring/rooms.md and docs/design/authoring/AI-GUIDE.md.

id.description: This room's id; must match the file path: rooms/<area>/<name>.room.json has id "room:<area>/<name>".

name.description: Human-readable name (not used by the game).

description.description: Free text: intent, notes for the next editor or model (not used by the game).

bind.description: Numeric ids in the game. Vanilla rooms carry them so they compile to the same slots; new rooms omit bind and the compiler allocates.

content.description: Index shared by the room's tilemap, collision, object, progress and nav tables (vanilla: 0-286).

size.description: Room size in 16-px cells. The fg tilemap is twice this in 8-px tiles. One screen is 15x10 cells.

area.description: New rooms only: the world area the game files the room under (the AI helpers' room graph and the pause screens' area lookup, gUnk_08D6CD0C.unk46). Default: the area of the vanilla room the first door leads to, else rainbow_route. Vanilla rooms ignore it (their area comes from the game).

extraBgOffsetX.description: Constant horizontal scroll offset of the extra layer (HW BG2), added after the parallax term in camera-parallax mode (priorityFlags bit 1 clear). The extra layer is never instantiated in retail data (objectList2Idx is 0xFFFF everywhere). Unit: px. Neutral value 0. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) Same as raw.unk02; omitted = 0.

extraBgOffsetY.description: Constant vertical offset of the extra layer (HW BG2): subtracted from its bottom-anchored scroll Y, so a positive value shows N more pixels of the layer's top (the image moves down on screen). Camera-parallax mode only. Code-only: the extra layer is never instantiated. Unit: px. Neutral value 0. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) Same as raw.unk04; omitted = 0.

extraBgScrollX.description: Extra layer (HW BG2) horizontal scroll parameter, dual-purpose: with priorityFlags bit 1 clear it is the parallax ratio (8.8, 0x100 = moves 1:1 with the camera); with bit 1 set it is added to the layer's scroll every frame (auto-scroll velocity). Copied to LevelInfo.unk_S16Vec2_B4.x at load. Note the C name is misleading: _06 is X, _08 is Y. Unit: fx8.8 ratio (bit1 clear) | fx8.8 px/frame (bit1 set). Neutral value 256. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) Same as raw.unkXmod_06; omitted = 256.

extraBgScrollY.description: Extra layer (HW BG2) vertical counterpart of unkXmod_06: parallax ratio (8.8) in camera mode, per-frame velocity with priorityFlags bit 1 set. Unit: fx8.8 ratio (bit1 clear) | fx8.8 px/frame (bit1 set). Neutral value 256. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) Same as raw.unkXmod_08; omitted = 256.

bgOffsetX.description: Constant horizontal offset of the background layer (HW BG0) in camera-parallax mode: bgScrollX = cameraX*ratio + unk0A. Original-code quirk: the load-time seed copies it WITHOUT the *0x100 (level.c:223), the per-frame formula with it; harmless because the next frame recomputes, and invisible because it is 0 everywhere. Keep the quirk when porting. Unit: px. Neutral value 0. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) Same as raw.unk0A; omitted = 0.

bgOffsetY.description: Vertical offset of the background layer (HW BG0). The background's scroll Y is anchored so that the background's bottom edge meets the screen's bottom edge when the camera is at the bottom of the room; unk0C is subtracted from that, so the background image sits unk0C pixels lower on screen (shows more of its top). Used both at load and every frame (camera-parallax mode). Unit: px. Neutral value 0. (registry confidence: confirmed) Same as raw.unk0C; omitted = 0.

bgScrollX.description: Background layer (HW BG0) horizontal scroll parameter. With priorityFlags bit 2 clear (camera-parallax mode, 285/286 rooms) it is the parallax ratio in 8.8 fixed point: 0x100 = the background moves 1:1 with the camera, 0x40 = a quarter as fast, 0 = fixed. -1 = derive it at load as (bgWidthPx - 240) / 2160, i.e. map 9 screen-widths of camera travel onto the background's full width (0x870 = 9 * 240). If the background is no wider than the screen the ratio is forced to 0. With bit 2 set it is instead added to the background's scroll every frame (auto-scroll velocity, 8.8 px/frame). Unit: fx8.8 ratio (bit2 clear) | fx8.8 px/frame (bit2 set). Neutral value -1. Special values: -1 = derive from background width: (bgWidthPx - 240) * 256 / 0x870. (registry confidence: confirmed) Same as raw.unk0E; omitted = -1.

bgScrollY.description: Background layer (HW BG0) vertical scroll parameter; same scheme as unk0E. Ratio mode: 8.8 ratio applied to the camera's distance from the room's bottom edge; -1 = derive as (bgHeightPx - 160) / 1440 (0x5A0 = 9 * 160); forced to 0 when the background is no taller than the screen. Velocity mode (priorityFlags bit 2): added to the scroll Y every frame. Unit: fx8.8 ratio (bit2 clear) | fx8.8 px/frame (bit2 set). Neutral value -1. Special values: -1 = derive from background height: (bgHeightPx - 160) * 256 / 0x5A0. (registry confidence: confirmed) Same as raw.unk10; omitted = -1.

playfieldBehindExtraLayer.description: BG priority: set -> playfield (BG3) priority 2 and extra layer (BG2) priority 1, so the extra layer draws in front of the playfield and the playfield drops behind priority-1 sprites; clear -> BG3 priority 1, BG2 priority 2. Set in every retail room (the extra layer never exists, so in practice it only sets the playfield's priority relative to sprites). The port renderer also reads it (platform/render/rl_build.c). Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: confirmed) (mask 0x0001)

extraBgAutoScroll.description: Extra layer (BG2): add unkXmod_06/08 to its scroll every frame instead of camera parallax. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) (mask 0x0002)

bgAutoScroll.description: Background layer (BG0): unk0E/unk10 are a per-frame scroll velocity instead of parallax ratios. Only room 919 (Dark Mind sky) sets it, with velocity 0/0: the room freezes the parallax so its own code (code_080023A4.c, case 919) can drive the background scroll directly. (registry confidence: confirmed) (mask 0x0004)

phoneCallAllowed.description: The cell phone works here: pressing R with battery calls the CPU helper Kirbys (sub_08056C2C, SE_KIRBY_CALL, consumes a battery), and the HUD shows the phone icon only in rooms with this bit. Clear only in room 919 and the credits rooms 980-982. (registry confidence: confirmed) (mask 0x0008)

answerCallAllowed.description: Responding to another Kirby's phone call works here: while a call is pending (gUnk_02021580 = caller's player id, set when the caller's call completes, kirby.c sub_080572A0), pressing R in a room other than the caller's (or when the caller is dead/out) warps this Kirby to the caller via sub_08056C2C; the HUD shows the incoming-call indicator only when this bit is set. Same rooms as bit 3 in retail data, so data cannot separate them; only the call sites do. (registry confidence: likely) (mask 0x0010)

returnToHubAllowed.description: Holding L returns Kirby to the hub: newly pressed L (unk11A & 0x200) enters sub_08056E40 (phone animation, SE_KIRBY_CALL, no battery cost, unkC |= 0x40000); holding L for 48 frames continues to sub_0805BEE8 -> sub_08057774, which sets roomId = 801 and warps. Clear in the hub/tutorial (801, 803-805), the final area (909-919), minigame/rematch rooms and the credits. (registry confidence: confirmed) (mask 0x0040)

roomFlags.description: Room behaviour bits. Misnamed in C: only bit 0 is about BG priority. Bits 1-2 select auto-scroll for the two background layers, bits 3/4/6 gate the cell-phone (R) and return-to-hub (L) actions. Retail data uses only 0x79 (262 rooms), 0x19 (11), 0x39 (9), 0x01 (3) and 0x25 (1). Exhaustive search of game/src for priorityFlags: masks 1, 2, 4, 8, 0x10, 0x40 only. Neutral value 121. (registry confidence: likely) Same as raw.priorityFlags.

props.description: Room properties with registry names (camera, parallax, flags). Empty until the semantics registry names them; use raw meanwhile.

raw.description: Room properties by their C field name, for fields the registry has not named. Always accepted, even after a field gets a name.

fgLayerRoomTag.description: Advanced: the room-id annotation in the playfield layer header; defaults to this room's numeric id.

art.description: The playfield art (HW BG3), one legend key per 16x16 cell. Each legend value is a metatile: four 8x8 tile tokens from the room's tileset. Art is separate from collision: what you see vs. what is solid.

collision.description: What each 16x16 cell is to physics, one legend key per cell. Conventional keys: "." empty, "#" solid, "=" one-way platform, "~" water, "^" hazard, "%" breakable, "D" door cell, "H" ladder; the legend decides.

patches.description: Cell changes the game applies at run time to a cell (e.g. a breakable block turning into air): new art and new collision for one cell. Several on one cell apply in order.

tiles.description: New art for the cell: TL TR BL BR.

key.description: Advanced: the collision value that selects this patch; derived from the grid (and earlier patches on the cell) when omitted.

doors.description: Door transitions: standing on one of `cells` and entering takes Kirby to `arrive` in room `to`. Order matters: it is the order of the per-room save bits (chests first, then doors), so append rather than reorder in an existing room. Most doors need a door-typed collision value under their cells and often a door object for the graphics.

arrive.description: Where Kirby arrives in the destination room, in 16-px cells: the cell he lands ON (in vanilla, the floor cell right under the destination door), so the cell above it must be empty.

cells.description: The cells of this room that act as the door.

flags.description: Door behaviour bits (Unk_0888562C_3.unk0C): 0x80 = do not move the respawn point; 0x01 / 0x02 = arrive facing one way / the other (docs/naming/doors.md). Omitted = 0.

cellFlags.description: Advanced: per-cell flags when they differ between cells of one door.

objects.description: Things placed in the room: enemies, items, chests, gadgets, triggers. Positions are pixels (cell * 16 + 8 is a cell centre). Order is the spawn order.

movePattern.description: Movement pattern, switched in CreateWaddleDee and again in sub_080A3CF0 (re-entry after landing / parasol loss). Values >4 fall to default = 0 (one retail record has 5). (registry confidence: confirmed) (template field subtype1)

speed.description: Runtime obj->subtype. Walking speed index for patterns 0/1/2 and the hop: subtype 0..3 -> |xspeed| 0x80/0xC0/0x100/0x180 (0.5/0.75/1/1.5 px per frame). For pattern 1 also the turn period. For pattern 3 it is passed to the parasol as its subtype1 and value 2 keeps the Dee standing after landing. Unit: enum index. (registry confidence: confirmed) (template field subtype2)

paletteVariant.description: Sprite palette variant (generic, object.c sub_0803DFAC). Value 1 on two walkers (subtype2 1 and 2). (registry confidence: likely) (template field unkF)

enemyFlags.description: Generic enemy flag word, read in object.c for every type 0x00-0x64 (ObjType0To37/38To52/53To64). bit0: on death (unk80<=0) the object adds 1 to the per-room-group kill counter gUnk_02023508[unk65E] (read back by OBJ_LEVER_WALL via unkF and by OBJ_OBJECT_SPAWNER). bit1: InitObject sets base.unkC |= 0x1000, which makes ProcessObjectCollisionLists resolve this object against the solid-object list (it is pushed by / can stand on solid objects such as blocks and platforms, like Kirby). bit2: on death, skip sub_08086C48 (the restore-room-music task used after mini-boss fights). bit15 (types 0x00-0x32 only): unkC |= 0x10, the 'Droppy' look: the palette of OBJ_DROPPY is used instead of the type's own. Type-specific code may read further bits. (registry confidence: likely) (template field unk22)

flightPattern.description: Flight pattern, switched in CreateBrontoBurt and in sub_080AD7C0 (resume after being stunned). Values >5 fall to default = 0. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype1)

fast.description: Runtime obj->subtype. Non-zero: horizontal flight speed 0x100 instead of 0xC0, follows a different scripted flight table in the post-rise/dash states; ==1 raises the diagonal-bounce speed from 0xB5 to 0xE2. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype2)

swimPattern.description: Swim pattern, switched in sub_080A712C (descriptor init, called from CreateBlipper via gUnk_08351648[type].unk10) and after re-entering water. Values >4 = 0. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype1)

fast.description: Runtime obj->subtype. Only read by the height-tracking state (pattern 0): non-zero doubles the vertical acceleration (0x18 vs 0xC) and raises the max speed (0x120 vs 0xC0). Retail values 2 and 3 sit on patterns 2 and 3, where nothing reads it. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype2)

fireRate.description: Runtime obj->subtype. 0: never shoots (only plays the 35-frame pulse). Non-zero: each cycle fires a burst of 5 OBJ_GLUNK_BULLETs 12 frames apart; the idle wait between bursts is (3 - subtype) animation loops, so 2 shoots more often than 1. Also copied to the bullet's subtype2. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype2)

movePattern.description: Pattern switch in CreateSquishy. Values >2 = 0. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype1)

fast.description: Runtime obj->subtype. Non-zero: swim 0xC0 instead of 0x80 and leap 0x140 instead of 0x100. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype2)

appearMode.description: 0: hovers in place (scripted bob, gUnk_08353510). Non-zero: hidden ambusher: invisible (flags 0x600) until Kirby is within 10 px horizontally, then reappears at a fixed offset from Kirby and flies vertically toward him; when level it hovers normally. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype1)

fastChase.description: Runtime obj->subtype. Non-zero selects the faster angry-chase state sub_080A7C0C (vertical accel 0x20, max 0x1C0) instead of sub_080A7A88 (0x10, 0x160). Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype2)

enemyFlags.description: Generic enemy flag word, read in object.c for every type 0x00-0x64 (ObjType0To37/38To52/53To64). bit0: on death (unk80<=0) the object adds 1 to the per-room-group kill counter gUnk_02023508[unk65E] (read back by OBJ_LEVER_WALL via unkF and by OBJ_OBJECT_SPAWNER). bit1: InitObject sets base.unkC |= 0x1000, which makes ProcessObjectCollisionLists resolve this object against the solid-object list (it is pushed by / can stand on solid objects such as blocks and platforms, like Kirby). bit2: on death, skip sub_08086C48 (the restore-room-music task used after mini-boss fights). bit15 (types 0x00-0x32 only): unkC |= 0x10, the 'Droppy' look: the palette of OBJ_DROPPY is used instead of the type's own. Type-specific code may read further bits. (registry confidence: likely) (template field unk22)

motion.description: Motion pattern switch in CreateGordo. Values >3 = 0. (registry confidence: confirmed) (template field subtype1)

speed.description: Runtime obj->subtype. Patrol speed for motions 1/2: 0xC0 + 0x40*subtype (0.75 px/frame + 0.25 per step). Unit: 0.25 px/frame steps above 0.75 px/frame. (registry confidence: confirmed) (template field subtype2)

paletteVariant.description: Sprite palette variant (generic). (registry confidence: likely) (template field unkF)

enemyFlags.description: Generic enemy flag word, read in object.c for every type 0x00-0x64 (ObjType0To37/38To52/53To64). bit0: on death (unk80<=0) the object adds 1 to the per-room-group kill counter gUnk_02023508[unk65E] (read back by OBJ_LEVER_WALL via unkF and by OBJ_OBJECT_SPAWNER). bit1: InitObject sets base.unkC |= 0x1000, which makes ProcessObjectCollisionLists resolve this object against the solid-object list (it is pushed by / can stand on solid objects such as blocks and platforms, like Kirby). bit2: on death, skip sub_08086C48 (the restore-room-music task used after mini-boss fights). bit15 (types 0x00-0x32 only): unkC |= 0x10, the 'Droppy' look: the palette of OBJ_DROPPY is used instead of the type's own. Type-specific code may read further bits. (registry confidence: likely) (template field unk22)

aiScript.description: Selects the input script stored in obj->unk7C in CreateChip. All four make Chip hop; they differ in facing and in whether hops carry horizontal motion. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype1)

Type-specific code may read further bits. (registry confidence: likely) (template field unk22)

flightPattern.description: Flight pattern chosen in sub_080AB8DC. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype1)

diveSpeed.description: Runtime obj->subtype, read only by the homing dive (subtype1 0): selects the top speed unk85 (0:0x30, 1:0x40, 2:0x60, 3:0x80, 4:0xA0, other: 0x30, in 1/256 of the unit direction*speed product) and adds subtype to the per-step acceleration (unk9E += 1 + subtype every frame). Value 5 (4 retail records, all subtype1 0) therefore = top speed 0x30 but fastest acceleration. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype2)

speedProfile.description: How xspeed evolves in flight (sub_080A0F2C, and sub_080A100C after being bounced). (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype1)

launchSpeed.description: Initial |xspeed| in sub_080A0E98: 0 -> 0x200, 1 -> 0x300, 2 -> 0x380, others -> 0 (fx8.8 px/frame). Unit: fx8.8 px/frame (enum). (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype2)

canJump.description: Boolean: when non-zero, the 'jump' input bit (unk9C & 1, set by the script when Kirby is within 0x50 px with 1/4 chance every 16 frames) makes it jump from idle/roll states; with 0 it only rolls. Unit: bool. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype1)

flightPattern.description: Selected in sub_080A2AF0 (the type's start function). (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype1)

shotDelayOrPasses.description: Runtime obj->subtype. subtype1 0: non-zero delays the first attack check to 270 frames instead of 90. subtype1 3: number of chase passes - 1 before leaving. Also passed as subtype2 of the spawned OBJ_CUPIE_ARROW (no reader of it found). (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype2)

Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype1)

hopScript.description: Runtime subtype; with subtype1=0 selects the hop motion table: 1 -> sub_080B0428 (gUnk_08353DBC), 2 -> sub_080B05C0 (gUnk_08353E58), other -> sub_080B0290 (gUnk_08353D20). Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype2)

(registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype1)

starSubtype.description: Runtime subtype; only passed on as subtype2 of the spawned OBJ_JACK_STAR. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype2)

cannonLockSlot.description: Room state slot (GetStateSlot(STATE_SLOT_ROOM, unk14)) set to 1 while Jack exists and cleared when it is destroyed; 0 = none. spawnMode.description: How the bonus enters play. 0 = placed: y is snapped down onto the 16-px cell floor, the twinkle sparkle is attached (unless unk22 bit 2) and it waits to be touched. The non-zero modes are used by run-time spawns (chests, enemies, Kirby), never by room data: 1 = hidden inside Kirby and popped out when his animation reaches 0x69; 2 = pops out upward (yspeed 0x180); 3 = created inert; 4 = sub_08123924. Any non-zero mode also blinks from frame 240 and despawns at frame 360. Every vanilla room uses the same value; other values reach code no shipped level exercises. (registry confidence: likely) (template field subtype2)

bonusFlags.description: Bit field. Bit 3 (8) is the only one the retail data uses heavily (~40% of placements): the item floats where it is placed, with no gravity and no terrain collision (ObjectBase flags 0x40 = no gravity, 0x100 = no tile collision; see ObjectMain). Without it the item drops to the floor. Bit 0 (generic, types 0..0x64) counts the pickup towards the room's "defeated" counter when the object dies with hp <= 0; bit 1 (generic) makes it collide with solid objects; bit 2 suppresses the twinkle sparkle. (registry confidence: confirmed) (template field unk22)

tileset.schema.json.title: katam foreground tileset (katam-tileset/1)
tileset.schema.json.description: The playfield's 8x8 tiles (VRAM char block 2) as an indexed PNG, 4 bits per pixel, 32 tiles per row; plus looping tile animations. The PNG palette is only a preview: pixel indices 0-15 are the data, colours come from the room's palette bank. Index 0 is transparent.

chunkStride.description: Tiles between chunks, source and destination (default 32 = one sheet row).

gfxTile.description: First tile of this frame in animImage.

metatile_attributes.json.description: A room collision cell (one u8 per 16x16 px, see solidity_map.json) is an index into gCollisionAttributes, a 256-entry table of u32 terrain words defined in C. The physics tests bits of the word; the editor should present the INDEX (that is what rooms store) with the decoded word as its meaning. Indices that share a word are still distinct (34-39 all equal index 13 but are used separately, e.g. matched by cell records), so never canonicalise an index by its word.
notes: Word layout: bits 0-15 property flags, 16-19 unused, 20-23 level (meaning depends on the flag), 24-27 forceDir, 28-31 slope enum.

values: 125 non-zero entries; 80 indices are placed in retail rooms; 45 non-zero entries (all water slopes 52-71, conveyors 103-108, droppable sloped platforms 16-19/24-25, diagonal currents 48-51, idx 73, idx 92, some wind/current variants) are never placed. Zero words (113-239, 248-251) are reserved, not air.
Long-form argument and per-site evidence: docs/naming/metatile-attributes.md (line numbers there are from an older tree).

fields.name: terrain
fields.description: terrain bitfield

bits.name: empty
bits.description: Passable: no blocking geometry. The per-tile collision handler (gUnk_082D8DA4) is dispatched only when this bit is clear; walkers treat an empty cell below the next step as a ledge. Index 0 (word 0x1) is plain air. A word of 0 is NOT air: it is an unused slot (113-239, 248-251).

evidence.note: handler dispatch only for non-empty tiles

evidence.data: index 0 (0x1) is 40.8% of all 293,674 retail cells; every placed index with a blocking bit lacks 0x1

bits.name: water
bits.description: Underwater: swimming physics, splash dust/SFX, selects the water force table for currents. Kirby keeps WATER|MINI_ONLY|DOOR across state resets (unk58 &= 0x4402).

evidence.note: slower movement in water
water current table instead of wind

evidence.data: index 72 (0x3): 8,248 cells in 50 rooms, contiguous regions

bits.name: topSolid
bits.description: One-way platform: collides only from above (landing registers only while moving down). With a slope nibble it is a sloped one-way platform.

evidence.note: floor contact only when moving downward
snap onto a flat top-solid tile

evidence.data: index 15 (0x4): 2,028 cells, runs 2.47 wide x 1.02 tall, air above and below 92%

bits.name: dropThrough
bits.description: On a topSolid tile: Kirby can press down to fall through it (sub_080035F4 requires empty-or-dropThrough under the feet and a dropThrough tile among them). Never appears without 0x4.

evidence.data: index 14 (0xC) mirrors index 15 (0x4) spatially; no spatial test separates them

bits.name: slippery
bits.description: Ice: ground friction drops (8 instead of 32, 13 instead of 27, 4 instead of 14 per anim state). Ignored while Kirby has the Ice ability.

evidence.data: only on floor slopes 74-79 and solid block 80; 9,629 cells in 30 rooms

bits.name: chainTrigger
bits.description: Breaking this block starts a chain explosion task (sub_0800E0E4) that eats adjacent chainMember cells, instead of spawning plain debris.

evidence.code: sub_0800E0E4((struct Object *)attack, column + tileX, row + tileY);

evidence.data: index 246 sits as a single cell on top of index-242 masses 100% of the time

bits.name: chainMember
bits.description: A chain explosion propagates into (and destroys) this cell; projectiles can tunnel through it.

evidence.note: propagation tests the neighbours for 0x40

evidence.data: index 242 (0x240): 4,074 cells in 131 rooms adjacent to triggers 241/246

bits.description: Never tested; set only on index 92, which no room places.

bits.name: ladder
bits.description: Climbable ladder/rope. Index 33 = rope body (empty|ladder), index 32 = ladder top (a drop-through platform that is also a ladder; compared as the whole word gCollisionAttributes[32]).

evidence.note: sub_08009D28: on a ladder
ladder top test
climb up stops when the cell above has no ladder

evidence.data: index 33 runs 1.00 wide x 3.99 tall; index 32 has index 33 below it 100%

bits.name: solid
bits.description: Full 16x16 solid block (walls, floors, ceilings). AI grid value 2.

bits.name: miniOnly
bits.description: Gap only Mini Kirby fits: any other Kirby inside it dies instantly (hp = 0); solid for the AI unless Mini.

evidence.data: index 89: 33 cells in 4 rooms, 3.67 wide x 1 tall, solid above and below 100%

bits.name: force
bits.description: Applies a directional push while inside the tile (wind / water current; conveyors exist in the table but no room uses them). Direction = forceDir nibble, strength = level (0..2) indexing gUnk_082D91A4 (air) or gUnk_082D91BC (water). Stone/Smash Kirby ignore updrafts.

evidence.data: vertical-force tiles form tall columns, horizontal ones wide bands (e.g. idx 85 up: 5.2 x 41.9)

bits.name: breakable
bits.description: Destructible block. Hardness = level field: 0-1 any attack, 2 needs attack flag unk68 & 0x1000, 3 needs 0x4000, 4 needs 0x800 (set by the giant star/stone block objects and one Kirby attack). Level-0 blocks are also broken by the weaker sweep (and pass thrown stars).

evidence.note: AI grid value 3 = destructible

evidence.data: levels 0-4 all placed: 240 (lvl0) 130 rooms, 241/244 (lvl1), 245 (2) 33 rooms, 246 (3) 13 rooms, 247 (4) 25 rooms

bits.name: hazard
bits.description: Damages Kirby on contact (1 HP, knock-back, loses ability). Level = damage element: 0 plain (spikes), 1 fire (burn animation 123, SE_KIRBY_FIRE_DMG), 2 a second element (animation 135, generic damage SFX; likely electric). Levels above 2 do not damage. ctor.code: void* CreateBonus(struct ObjectTemplate* arg0, u8 arg1) {

0x5E.description: Small food: restores a little HP. Collectable consumable; touching it applies the effect. Collecting a placed one (unk2/unk3 not the default) adds 1 to the room's collected counter gUnk_02023510.

params.name: appearance
params.description: Small food only: copied to unk83, the sprite variant (which food is drawn).

params.name: spawnMode
params.description: How the bonus enters play. 0 = placed: y is snapped down onto the 16-px cell floor, the twinkle sparkle is attached (unless unk22 bit 2) and it waits to be touched. The non-zero modes are used by run-time spawns (chests, enemies, Kirby), never by room data: 1 = hidden inside Kirby and popped out when his animation reaches 0x69; 2 = pops out upward (yspeed 0x180); 3 = created inert; 4 = sub_08123924. Any non-zero mode also blinks from frame 240 and despawns at frame 360.

0.name: placed
0.description: static pickup, snapped to the floor cell

evidence.note: placed: snap to floor
non-zero modes time out at 360 frames

evidence.data: subtype2 is 0 in every retail placement of 0x5E..0x64

params.name: bonusFlags
params.description: Bit field. Bit 3 (8) is the only one the retail data uses heavily (~40% of placements): the item floats where it is placed, with no gravity and no terrain collision (ObjectBase flags 0x40 = no gravity, 0x100 = no tile collision; see ObjectMain). Without it the item drops to the floor. Bit 0 (generic, types 0..0x64) counts the pickup towards the room's "defeated" counter when the object dies with hp <= 0; bit 1 (generic) makes it collide with solid objects; bit 2 suppresses the twinkle sparkle.

bits.name: countsAsDefeat
bits.description: Generic for types 0x00..0x64: when the object is destroyed with unk80 (hp) <= 0, add 1 to the room's defeat counter gUnk_02023508 (read by OBJ_OBJECT_SPAWNER and OBJ_TRIGGERABLE_WALL). On a bonus this is effectively inert: collecting sets the counter-B (collected) path instead.

evidence.data: set on 1-2 items (rooms 823, 121, 202, 414), all otherwise ordinary

bits.name: collidesWithSolidObjects
bits.description: Generic for types 0x00..0x64: sets ObjectBase.unkC 0x1000, which makes ResolveSolidObjectCollision push this object out of solid objects (blocks).

bits.name: noSparkle
bits.description: Do not attach the twinkle effect (sprite 0x2BB) to a placed item.

bits.name: floating
bits.description: Float in place: no gravity, no tile collision. Clear = falls to the ground and rests on it.

evidence.note: no gravity (object.c sub_0809D1E0 skips yspeed -= 5)
gravity only when flag 0x40 clear
tile collision only when flag 0x100 clear

params.description: Not read by CreateBonus or any bonus state function (no reader in game/src for this type). The rare 256/512 values look like leftovers of the enemy record the item was copied from.

evidence.data: unk18 is 0 except one 256 on each of 0x5E, 0x61, 0x63 and one 512 on 0x62

evidence.note: the only unk2x/unk1x reads in bonus.c are subtype2/subtype1/unk22

object_template.json.description: One placed object in a room's object list (gLevelObjLists[objectListIdx]->unk0, see object_lists.json). The list is walked by stride (unk1) until a zero stride. The header fields below have one meaning for every type; from subtype1 on, fields are per-type parameters documented in object_params.json (the descriptions here give only the generic part).
notes: 3,482 records in 287 lists (longest 30); every retail record is 36 bytes with spawnTable 1 and unkA/unkB/unkD = 0xFF.

Spawning: CreateLevelObjects and the two scroll-in walks (game/src/code_080023A4.c ~5914-6014) skip an object whose despawn flag (unk2, unk3) is set, and, unless unk5 bit 0 is set, objects outside the spawn window around the viewport; CreateObject then calls gSpawnFuncTable{spawnTable}[type](template, playerId).
Positions: x/y are pixels, InitObject turns them into 8.8 world coordinates; object placement is free (not cell-snapped), though most retail values are multiples of 8.

fields.name: size
fields.description: Byte stride to the next record; 0 terminates the list. Always 36 in retail data, but the walker honours any value, so a record may carry extra trailing bytes.

fields.name: despawnScope
fields.description: Which 'already collected / defeated' bitmap unk3 indexes. If the bit is set the object is not spawned. 0 = per room visit (cleared on every room load, 32 bits), 1 = per area (cleared on area change, warp star and some Kirby transitions; used by all food/battery/1UP pickups so they stay collected while you remain in the area), 2 = saved with the file (never used by level data).

notes: gUnk_08D640A4[RoomProps.doorsIdx] (0x08D640A4, 287 pointers) -> the room's progress checklist: the chests and doors that count for the area map, and the bit positions they own in the saved gVisitedDoors[doorsIdx] word.

gVisitedDoors[doorsIdx] (u16, saved in the world-props SRAM block, game/src/save.c): bit i = entry i done (chest collected / door used), bit 15 = room visited. The area map shows a room as completed when all chest bits are set.

The three walkers (sub_08002B30 / sub_08002BA8 / sub_08002C18) loop for(;;) until they find a matching entry and never test the terminator: a chest or door whose key is missing from its room's list hangs the game. An editor must keep exactly one tag-2 entry per logical door (559 in retail = the distinct (destRoom, destX, destY) triples among the 724 tag-3 door cells) and one tag-1 entry per chest object (84), chests first.
Retail: 643 entries, all stride 8, chests always the leading chestCount entries (286/286 lists), list length 0..11, terminator = 4 bytes {0, 0, 0xFF, 0xFF}.

room_props.json.description: Per-room properties: music, background scrolling (parallax) for the two background layers, room behaviour flags, and the indices into the nine per-room content tables. Read by FillLevelInfo (game/src/level.c) at room load and by the per-frame BG scroll update sub_08001408's caller in game/src/code_080023A4.c.
notes: 983 slots, 286 real rooms (ids 101..982); the other 697 are all-0xFFFF filler. A tool must test each slot, not stop at the first filler.

In all 286 retail rooms mapDataIdx == solidityMapIdx == objectListIdx == unk22 == doorsIdx, and pixelDataIdx == paletteDataIdx in 258. The game reads each one separately, so an editor may keep them equal (one 'content index' per room) but must write all five.

Layer map (docs/naming/room-tables.md): HW BG3 = playfield (gForegroundTilemaps[mapDataIdx], scroll = camera); HW BG0 = background (gRoomTiledBGs[backgroundIdx], scroll = altViewport_34, driven by unk0A/unk0C/unk0E/unk10); HW BG2 = an 'extra layer' (gLevelObjLists[objectList2Idx] read as RoomTiledBG, scroll = altViewport_24, driven by unk02/unk04/unkXmod_06/unkXmod_08) that no retail room instantiates.

Parallax maths, per frame (game/src/code_080023A4.c ~850-895), in pixels: bgScrollX = cameraX * ratioX/256 + offsetX; bgScrollY = (bgHeight - 160) - (roomHeight - 160 - cameraY) * ratioY/256 - offsetY. X is anchored at the room's left edge, Y at its bottom edge.

fields.name: music
fields.description: Song number started when the local player enters the room (m4aSongNumStartOrChange: if that song is already playing it continues, so neighbouring rooms with the same value do not restart the music). Copied to the per-room-slot gUnk_02023518 at load (GetRoomMusicId/SetRoomMusicId let objects override it later, e.g. bosses). 0 = MUS_DUMMY, i.e. silence; used by the boss rooms x00 and the final-area rooms 909-918, whose music is started by the boss/cutscene object instead. Room 801 with gAIKirbyState < NORMAL stops all music instead of playing it.

fields.name: extraBgScrollX

Copied to LevelInfo.unk_S16Vec2_B4.x at load. Note the C name is misleading: _06 is X, _08 is Y.

fields.name: bgOffsetX
fields.description: Constant horizontal offset of the background layer (HW BG0) in camera-parallax mode: bgScrollX = cameraX*ratio + unk0A. Original-code quirk: the load-time seed copies it WITHOUT the *0x100 (level.c:223), the per-frame formula with it; harmless because the next frame recomputes, and invisible because it is 0 everywhere. Keep the quirk when porting.

fields.name: bgOffsetY
fields.description: Vertical offset of the background layer (HW BG0). The background's scroll Y is anchored so that the background's bottom edge meets the screen's bottom edge when the camera is at the bottom of the room; unk0C is subtracted from that, so the background image sits unk0C pixels lower on screen (shows more of its top). Used both at load and every frame (camera-parallax mode).

fields.name: bgScrollX
fields.description: Background layer (HW BG0) horizontal scroll parameter. With priorityFlags bit 2 clear (camera-parallax mode, 285/286 rooms) it is the parallax ratio in 8.8 fixed point: 0x100 = the background moves 1:1 with the camera, 0x40 = a quarter as fast, 0 = fixed. -1 = derive it at load as (bgWidthPx - 240) / 2160, i.e. map 9 screen-widths of camera travel onto the background's full width (0x870 = 9 * 240). If the background is no wider than the screen the ratio is forced to 0. With bit 2 set it is instead added to the background's scroll every frame (auto-scroll velocity, 8.8 px/frame).
fields.unit: fx8.8 ratio (bit2 clear) | fx8.8 px/frame (bit2 set)

evidence.note: x2 = (bgWidthPx - 240) << 8
background not wider than the screen: no horizontal parallax
camera * ratio / 256
velocity mode (priorityFlags & 4)

evidence.data: -1 in 87 rooms, otherwise small positive values 0..147 (64 in 38, 128 in 37, 32 in 23): ratios below 1.0 = background slower than the camera, textbook parallax

fields.name: bgScrollY
fields.description: Background layer (HW BG0) vertical scroll parameter; same scheme as unk0E. Ratio mode: 8.8 ratio applied to the camera's distance from the room's bottom edge; -1 = derive as (bgHeightPx - 160) / 1440 (0x5A0 = 9 * 160); forced to 0 when the background is no taller than the screen. Velocity mode (priorityFlags bit 2): added to the scroll Y every frame.
fields.unit: fx8.8 ratio (bit2 clear) | fx8.8 px/frame (bit2 set)

evidence.note: bottom-anchored: ratio applies to distance from the room bottom

evidence.data: -1 in 264 rooms; 0 in 910/912/914/916/919 (background fixed vertically); 17..106 in 17 rooms

fields.name: roomFlags
fields.description: Room behaviour bits. Misnamed in C: only bit 0 is about BG priority. Bits 1-2 select auto-scroll for the two background layers, bits 3/4/6 gate the cell-phone (R) and return-to-hub (L) actions. Retail data uses only 0x79 (262 rooms), 0x19 (11), 0x39 (9), 0x01 (3) and 0x25 (1). Exhaustive search of game/src for priorityFlags: masks 1, 2, 4, 8, 0x10, 0x40 only.

bits.name: playfieldBehindExtraLayer
bits.description: BG priority: set -> playfield (BG3) priority 2 and extra layer (BG2) priority 1, so the extra layer draws in front of the playfield and the playfield drops behind priority-1 sprites; clear -> BG3 priority 1, BG2 priority 2. Set in every retail room (the extra layer never exists, so in practice it only sets the playfield's priority relative to sprites). The port renderer also reads it (platform/render/rl_build.c).

bits.name: extraBgAutoScroll
bits.description: Extra layer (BG2): add unkXmod_06/08 to its scroll every frame instead of camera parallax.

bits.name: bgAutoScroll
bits.description: Background layer (BG0): unk0E/unk10 are a per-frame scroll velocity instead of parallax ratios. Only room 919 (Dark Mind sky) sets it, with velocity 0/0: the room freezes the parallax so its own code (code_080023A4.c, case 919) can drive the background scroll directly.

room-919 special case drives altViewport_34 itself

evidence.data: set only in room 919 (value 0x25), where unk0E = unk10 = 0

bits.name: phoneCallAllowed
bits.description: The cell phone works here: pressing R with battery calls the CPU helper Kirbys (sub_08056C2C, SE_KIRBY_CALL, consumes a battery), and the HUD shows the phone icon only in rooms with this bit. Clear only in room 919 and the credits rooms 980-982.

notes: gSolidityMaps[RoomProps.solidityMapIdx] (0x08D63330, 287 pointers) -> struct SolidityMap: the room's collision grid plus a list of per-cell records.

The cell-record list is walked by sub_080025AC with NO terminator test: it searches for the record whose (cellValue, x, y) equals the live collision cell and loops forever if none exists. Every code path that calls it (block breaking, door objects, Kirby door transitions) must therefore find its record: a breakable block or door cell without a record hangs the game. docs/naming/warp-hang.md is a real instance.

Retail data: 9500 tag-1 records, 724 tag-3 records, 0 tag-2 records; every list ends with a record whose stride is 0. 10142 of 10224 record keys equal the room's initial collision value at (x, y); the other 82 key on a value the cell only takes after an earlier patch (chained changes, e.g. a hidden door revealed by a switch: 40 records turn air into door index 255).

Door cells: 724 tag-3 records across 559 distinct (destRoom, destX, destY) triples: a door is usually 2 vertically adjacent cells, one logical door. progress_list.json holds exactly one tag-2 entry per logical door, and the two must stay paired.

records.description: Per-room collision grid and cell-record list.

Each byte is an index into gCollisionAttributes (metatile_attributes.json). Decompressed into gUnk_02024ED0[roomSlot] (1950 bytes per slot: the hard size cap for a room: (w/16)*(h/16) <= 1950).

notes: Three tables describe a room's two live BG layers: gForegroundTilemaps[mapDataIdx] (playfield size + tilemap only), gForegroundInfo[pixelDataIdx] (playfield tileset + tile animations), gForegroundPalettes[paletteDataIdx] (playfield palette + palette animations), and gRoomTiledBGs[backgroundIdx] (the background layer: everything in one RoomTiledBG).

Playfield tileset is LZ77-decompressed to char block 2 (0x06008000); background tileset to char block 0 (0x06000000). Playfield tilemap is LZ77-decompressed to EWRAM; background tilemap is used in place (uncompressed u16 screen entries).
A 'room id' tail field (RoomTiledBG.unk1C high half, ForegroundInfo.roomId, ForegroundPalette.roomId) is an authoring annotation the engine never reads: the first room that uses the entry.

records.description: A tiled BG layer. In gForegroundTilemaps only width, height, tilemap and unk1C are filled (tiles/palette come from ForegroundInfo/ForegroundPalette); in gRoomTiledBGs all fields are used. Copied whole into LevelInfo.unk180[layer] at room load.

items.what: starting hp by number of human players (1..4)
items.notes: ROM table at 0x08351530 (27 x 4 x s16), not yet a manifest kind: add 'boss_hp'. obj_desc.unk4 is ignored for these types. Rows 0x40..0x44 (empty types) are 2.

items.subject: Dark Mind form 1 (0x4F)
items.what: hp per encounter (placement subtype2 0..3) and player count

locations.note: forced to the last row when gUnk_0203AD10 & 4

items.notes: ROM table at 0x08351608, s16[8][4]: rows 0..3 are hp; rows 4..7 equal 0x4000/hp of rows 0..3 (a HUD scale like gUnk_08351458) but no reader of rows 4..7 was found.

items.subject: bosses
items.what: HUD hp-bar scale per boss and player count
items.notes: Every entry is floor(0x4000 / boss.hp) for the same cell (checked against the ROM). A mod that edits boss hp must regenerate it, or the bar will be wrong: make the pack compiler derive it.

items.subject: bosses
items.what: phase change at half hp (some bosses also at 1/4 and 3/4)

locations.note: subtype (placement subtype2) != 0 forces the second phase

items.notes: Derived from boss.hp (>>1, >>2) with the row index as a literal in each file. Quirk: dark_meta_knight.c uses row 0x10 (Gobbler's) for all its thresholds, not its own row 0x16 (the hp it starts with): editing DMK's hp does not move its phase points. Mr Frosty, Box Boxer and Crazy Hand have no hp-based phase; they only use subtype.

items.subject: bosses
items.what: attack choice odds, wind-up / cooldown timers, speeds
items.notes: Every boss file is a state machine with literal counters and RandLessThan / Rand16()&N odds (Dark Mind: ~100 Rand sites). Some movement is in motion-script tables (Kracko, Batafire, Gobbler, Bombar: see enemy.motion_scripts).

items.subject: bosses
items.what: song played when the fight starts
items.notes: Small C table; trivially data.

items.subject: bosses 0x43..0x52
items.what: what defeating a boss does (mirror shard drop, positions)
items.notes: Each handler hard-codes shard number and drop position (e.g. x=0x80, y=0x50). Progress logic, not tuning.

items.subject: boss attack objects
items.what: damage of boss projectiles/attacks
items.notes: As for enemies: per attack constructor. Nearly all are 1, so a per-type field would cover most of them.

{
  "format": "katam-project/1",
  "id": "examples.rainbow_annex",
  "name": "Rainbow Annex (example)",
  "description": "Four original rooms on top of the vanilla game in the style of Rainbow Route, hand-composed from its own pieces (CC0): trailhead (forest) -> cliffside (vertical climb) -> hollow (side room with a chest) and pine hills (lumber-yard look) -> one-way exit onto the left door of Rainbow Route 115. Entering: the trailhead's left door leads back to Rainbow Route 101; a natural entrance is a door added to 101 on its flat starting ground (around cell 5,8, before the first hill), arriving at the trailhead's left door: arrive {x: 4, y: 9}. Not included here, because that means copying room 101's tilemap into the project.",
  "base": "vanilla",
  "authors": [
    "katam-port"
  ],
  "license": "CC0-1.0"
}
